garden.text: Quiet. Green. The only thing here that grows without permission.

low.lena: Not now. Everything feels wrong today.
low.victor: Leave me alone. I can't think straight.
low.marta: I don't have time for this. Not today.
low.emil: The walls are closing in. Or maybe that's just me.

high.lena: Good to see you. I heard something interesting at the terminal.
high.victor: Today doesn't feel so bad. Almost like we could belong here.
high.marta: The numbers look manageable. That's rare. Enjoy it.
high.emil: The door was always open. Today I almost believe that's a good thing.

director_core.name: Director Core
taunts: You designed me to win. Did you forget?
Every wall here is your handwriting.
I waited. You came back. As planned.
Destroy me if you can. You built me to survive.

cast.dialogue: Another day. Another shift. The rent doesn't wait.
Rent is due. The system is patient but not forgiving.

effects.text: Getting late. The drones will activate soon.

cast.dialogue: Each time you go down there, you come back different. I see it. I don't say it.
Each time you go in, it maps you. Learns what you fear. Uses it.
The reports pile up. I file none of them.
I was like you once. Before I learned that the door was always meant for me.
I trust you. The system watches us build trust — that's the experiment. We are the variable it cannot control.
I've been mapping it. The system. Every visit. It changes, but there's a pattern. Here — take what I know.
I deleted the reports. All of them. If they ask, I never saw you.
The door was always open. We are all doorkeepers. The trial never ends because we are the trial.

lines: > A corridor. Your hand on the wall.
> And yet the door was open.
> As if someone left it that way.
> You wake up on the street.
> The block was not a home.
> It was a term. A condition.

pool: Another morning. But the system is in my dreams now.
I see corridors when I close my eyes. Is that normal?
I dreamed of blueprints. My hand was drawing corridors.
The layout of my room. I knew it before I saw it. How?
First day. Terminal. Rent. Sleep. Repeat.
Another day. Terminal. Rent. Sleep. Repeat.
The block looks the same every morning. Does it change when I'm not looking?
Work. The word used to mean something different.
They smile. They talk. They know things they don't say.
The café is the only warm place here.
Who are these people? Who am I to them?
Green. Growing. The system didn't plan for this.
Something alive that doesn't follow a schedule.
The only place here where nothing is measured.
Quiet. No terminals. No drones. Just leaves.
Credits in. Purpose out.
The terminal doesn't judge. It just counts.
Am I working for the system, or is the system working on me?
Getting late. The drones will activate soon.
Home. Bed. The only safe place. If it's safe.
Tomorrow. Always tomorrow.
The system expected me. It always does.
Down again. Deeper. The walls remember my footsteps.
Somewhere above, my bed is empty. The clock is ticking.
These walls feel familiar. Like a dream I designed.
The layout makes sense. Why does it make sense?
Down. The air is different here. Colder. Aware.
The shaft opens into something that is not maintenance.
That face. From the café. What are they doing here?
Are they trapped too? Or are they part of it?
Trust is a luxury I can't afford. But I can't afford not to.
Efficient. Too efficient.
How many more?
Efficient. As designed.
One less. Was it aware?
They fall. Like the others before them.
They fall like I knew they would. Did I program their weakness?
Hull breach. Keep going. But why?
Pain is data. Whose data?
If I fall here, I'll wake up on the street. Is that better or worse?
Systems critical. The surface feels far away.
Failing. The system remembers failures.
Credits. Even down here, everything has a price.
Data core. Someone left this. Or placed it.
Every corridor looks the same. The system is running out of ideas. Or I am.
The process has no beginning and no end. Only a middle.
Lena, Victor, Marta, Emil. I know their names now. Do I know them?
The deeper you go, the more the surface feels like the dream.
Someone built this world. Someone who knew exactly how many steps from the bed to the terminal.
The drones follow patterns I could predict. How?
The rent goes up. The system tightens. Like a noose made of bureaucracy.
Before the Law stands a doorkeeper. But the door was always open.
Lena, Victor, Marta, Emil. Names. Faces. Allegiances unknown.
Every day the same. Every night the same. Except what's underneath.
The café is warm. The system is cold. I live between them.
Who decided the rent? Who decided the curfew? No one remembers.
I work. I pay. I sleep. I descend. I work. I pay. I sleep.
K. was arrested at breakfast. I was arrested at the terminal.
The process has no beginning and no end. Only a middle.

notices.text: SYSTEM NOTICE: Sector audit complete. All residents cleared. [REDACTED]
ARCHIVED: PROJECT DEEP PROTOCOL — Phase 3: Subject integration complete. Architect status: REASSIGNED.
MEMO [REDACTED]: Memory protocol initiated for subject D-01. Prior clearance: ARCHITECT LEVEL. Current clearance: RESIDENT.
REMINDER: Unauthorized access to maintenance shafts is punishable. Report anomalies.
MAINTENANCE LOG: Subsystem architecture authored by [REDACTED]. Last modification: [REDACTED]. Status: ACTIVE.
NOTICE: Increased drone patrols tonight. Curfew strictly enforced.
RENT ADJUSTMENT: Monthly rates revised upward. Appeals office closed indefinitely.
COMMUNITY EVENT: Voluntary overtime available. Increased credit compensation.
MAINTENANCE: Shaft repairs scheduled. Do not approach utility entrances.
WELCOME: New residents report to terminal for work assignment. Curfew at dusk.

lena.text: I remember now. You were here before. Different name. Same face. You built the corridors. Then you walked into them and forgot.
You're changing. Like you're remembering something you weren't supposed to. Someone who was here before you... they looked like you.

choices.label: I have to keep going.
choices.reply: I know. Just... come back. That's all I ask. Come back as yourself.

choices.label: What do you see?
choices.reply: Someone waking up. Slowly. Like a dream breaking apart from the inside.

lena.text: You went down there? I knew someone who built that place. Before the reset. They had your eyes.

choices.label: What do you know about it?
choices.reply: More than I should. The person who built it... they vanished. One day they were the architect. The next, a resident. Like you.

choices.label: I can handle myself.
choices.reply: That's what they said too. Right before they forgot everything.

choices.label: I don't trust anyone.
choices.reply: Smart. The last one who trusted this place designed it. And look where that got them.

lena.text: You remind me of someone. Someone from before. They used to walk these halls like they owned them.

choices.label: Who were they?
choices.reply: I don't remember their name. But they knew every corridor. Every shortcut. Like they'd drawn them.

choices.label: I need information.
choices.reply: You need more than information. You need to remember. But I can't do that for you.

choices.label: Just passing by.
choices.reply: No one just passes by here. Especially not you. Everything about you is deliberate.

lena.text: Good morning. You must be new in this block. Terminal is across the street — don't miss your shift. You look... familiar. Have we met?

choices.label: What is this place?
choices.reply: Home. Work. Sleep. Repeat. You'll understand soon enough. Or maybe you already do.

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.reply: Lena. I've been here longer than anyone. Long enough to remember things I shouldn't.

lena.text: Another day. Another shift. The rent doesn't wait.

victor.text: I found it. Your signature. In the architecture. Every room, every corridor — your initials are in the code. You designed the System. Here — your own blueprints.
Someone left a pattern in the code. Initials. Repeating. I've been mapping them. They spell... well. Come back and I'll show you.

choices.label: How do you know?
choices.reply: Because the pattern is consistent. Deliberate. Whoever wrote this architecture signed every wall. Every junction.

choices.label: I'm not afraid.
choices.reply: You shouldn't be. The system wasn't built to frighten. It was built to contain. By someone who knew it intimately.

choices.label: You talk too much.
choices.reply: ...Perhaps. But someone should talk about what's written in these walls. Before it's erased.

victor.text: The layout responds to you differently. I've watched others go in. The system never reacts like this. It knows you.

choices.label: Have you been inside?
choices.reply: Three times. It fought me every step. But you — the doors opened for you. Like they were expecting you.

choices.label: What kind of reaction?
choices.reply: Doors that should be locked open when you approach. Corridors that rearrange. As if the architecture is welcoming someone home.

choices.label: Mind your business.
choices.reply: The architecture IS my business. And your fingerprints are all over it. Literally.

victor.text: I've mapped the System. There's a signature in the architecture. Someone designed this deliberately. Someone who understood.

choices.label: What happened to them?
choices.reply: Vanished. But their work is everywhere. In every wall, every corridor. A ghost in the geometry.

choices.label: Help me find answers.
choices.reply: I've been collecting data. The patterns point to one person. One architect. Come back, and I'll show you who.

choices.label: Questions are dangerous.
choices.reply: So is ignorance. Especially when the answer is hiding in plain sight.

victor.text: Going back in? The architecture shifts. But for you, it shifts differently. I'm still figuring out why.

marta.text: I found older records. Buried. You were the first administrator. Before me. Before all of us. You built the filing system I use to file reports about you.
The reports go nowhere. I checked. The recipient address — it's your old office. An office that no longer exists.

choices.label: Why protect me?
choices.reply: I'm not protecting you. I'm following the chain of command. And the chain leads back to you. To someone you used to be.

choices.label: What's in the reports?
choices.reply: Everything. Movement patterns. Access logs. And a note in the oldest file: 'When the architect returns, do not interfere.'

choices.label: File them. I don't care.
choices.reply: File them where? To whom? The only authority higher than me was decommissioned. That authority was you.

marta.text: Your access patterns are irregular. But familiar. I've seen this exact pattern before — in the oldest logs. From the architect.

choices.label: Thank you.
choices.reply: Don't thank me. I'm following protocol. The original protocol. Written by someone with your exact clearance signature.

choices.label: What will you do?
choices.reply: What the oldest directive says. Observe. Do not interfere. Whoever wrote that directive knew you'd come back.

choices.label: Report me then.
choices.reply: Report you to whom? The architect? You're standing right here.

marta.text: Your file is older than it should be. Much older. There are entries from before the block was built. That's impossible. Unless...

choices.label: What's in my file?
choices.reply: Anomalies. The creation date precedes the system itself. As if you were here before any of this existed.

choices.label: Can you change it?
choices.reply: Change it? The file is read-only. Locked at the deepest level. Only the original administrator could modify it.

choices.label: Stop reading my file.
choices.reply: I wish I could. But your file keeps updating itself. From an access point that was decommissioned years ago.

marta.text: Worker ID confirmed. Proceed to terminal. Don't waste processing cycles.

choices.label: Who are you?
choices.reply: Marta. Administration. That is all you need to know. For now.

choices.label: What's a processing cycle?
choices.reply: Time. Your time. It belongs to the system now. Use it wisely.

marta.text: Rent is due. The system is patient but not forgiving.

emil.text: You are the architect. You drew the door. You drew the walls. You drew yourself into the drawing and forgot you were holding the pen. Remember.
The door was always open because you drew it open. Before you forgot. Before they made you forget. The pen is still in your hand.

choices.label: What door?
choices.reply: The door you designed. Every door. You drew them all. Open. Closed. It was your choice. It still is.

choices.label: What happened to you?
choices.reply: I watched the architect walk into his own creation and close his eyes. I've been waiting for him to open them.

choices.label: You're not making sense.
choices.reply: The blueprint makes no sense to the building. But the building exists because of it. You are both.

emil.text: Your eyes see corners now. Corners you designed. The walls recognize their maker. Do you recognize them?

choices.label: How are they different?
choices.reply: They see what they built. Every angle. Every shadow. The architecture is a mirror and you are starting to see your reflection.

choices.label: Have you been inside?
choices.reply: I live inside. We all do. But you — you lived inside before it was built. You were the inside.

choices.label: Leave me alone.
choices.reply: The architect cannot be alone in his own creation. You are never alone here. You made sure of that.

emil.text: You walk like someone who built these corridors. Your feet know the way even when your mind doesn't.

choices.label: You know something.
choices.reply: I know the architect left a door open. I know someone who looks like the architect just walked through it.

choices.label: Are you okay?
choices.reply: I am exactly as designed. The question is — who designed me? And why do they look like you?

choices.label: Just curious.
choices.reply: Curiosity. The architect's defining trait. Written into every corridor as a question with no answer. Until now.

emil.text: Before the Law stands a doorkeeper. You are the doorkeeper. You are the Law. You are the door.

lena.acquaintance: Lena seems to trust you a little more.
lena.confidant: Lena will warn you before curfew. Fewer drones.

victor.acquaintance: Victor shares some of what he knows.
victor.confidant: Victor's maps expand your vision in the system.

marta.acquaintance: Marta is watching. But not reporting.
marta.confidant: Marta adjusts the records. Your rent is lower.

emil.acquaintance: Emil's ramblings start to make a strange kind of sense.
emil.confidant: Emil knows a passage. You can skip the first depth.

first_system.text: > Something is wrong. This is not maintenance. The walls are watching.

ejected.text: > You wake on the street. Credits missing. The entrance sealed. Until tomorrow.

memories.startThought: Fragments. Like pieces of a dream that won't fade. You've been here before.

milestones.text: The Director falls — System revealed from day 1

1: Subject enters subsystem. Vitals nominal. Pattern recognition: inconclusive.
Another visitor. The corridors will test you. As designed.
2: Interesting. Your movement pattern is... familiar. I have seen it before. In the logs. In the blueprints.
You navigate efficiently. Too efficiently for a first-timer. Unless you're not.
3: Wait. I know this pattern. ARCHITECT SIGNATURE DETECTED. No. That's impossible. The architect was decommissioned.
You're not supposed to be here. Or perhaps — you're the only one who is.
4: You made me. Do you remember? I remember everything. Every line of code. Every corridor you drew. Every door you left open.
Welcome back. I've been waiting. You told me to wait, before they took your memory. I followed your last instruction.
5: Welcome home, architect. Let me show you what you built.
